title: Soldier testimony sheds light on how Israel wages information war
subhead: One year after the bombing that killed 22 people, including five journalists, at Nasser Hospital in the south of the Gaza Strip, an Israeli soldier has told several media outlets, including Le Monde, how the Israeli army pulls out all stops to link bombing victims to Hamas.

title: 'The far right's current success in claiming the heritage of Charles de Gaulle should serve as a warning'
subhead: With eight months to go before the presidential election, and as Charles de Gaulle is celebrated on the big screen, documentary filmmaker Jonathan Hayoun observes the general's memory has become a legacy to be claimed and warns against letting the far right seize it to rewrite its own history.

title: Retro 'sunflower' pools bring nostalgia to Paris region and beyond
subhead: 'Aquatic Monuments' (5/6). The Tournesol pool, an emblem of prefabricated and modular architecture, spread throughout France in the 1970s, leaving its mark on generations of swimmers with its flying saucer-like appearance. Built in 1976, the Raymond-Mulinghausen pool in Les Lilas, on the edge of Paris, still welcomes swimmers in an almost unchanged setting.

title: One month after a megafire ravaged this French town, an unprecedented spirit of solidarity has taken hold
subhead: Between July 21 and August 1, a fire in southwest France swept through 42,000 hectares and destroyed 240 homes, mostly in Le Porge.

title: Unprecedented crisis grips US colleges, squeezed by soaring costs and Trump-fuelled distrust
subhead: Around 15 higher education institutions closed in 2025 due to debt, and about 40 closed in 2024. In addition to cuts in government funding, academia faced a decline in enrollment as many young people questioned the value of the skills taught.

title: 'Citizens no longer trusted us': Belgium's attempt to revive democracy
subhead: 'Room for Hope' (1/6). High voter abstention, unfulfilled political promises and the growing influence of authoritarian movements have weakened democracies. In response to this crisis, Belgian writer David Van Reybrouck is behind numerous initiatives that hope to reinvigorate democratic practice.
